paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the accuracy of different probing configurations across various perturbation setups applied to multilingual BERT models, comparing random and trained model variants. The horizontal axis contains categorical labels representing different perturbation conditions, arranged from left to right as: "embedding," "1st layer," "random layers," "random layers +B₂," "random layers +L₂," "random layers +R₂," "random layers +permute," "random," "random +B₂," "random +L₂," "random +R₂," "random +permute," and "unperturbed." The vertical axis is labeled "Accuracy" with a linear scale ranging from 70 to approximately 92, with tick marks at intervals of 5. Each category features a pair of bars — a lighter-colored bar and a darker-colored bar — representing two different random or model conditions. The blue bars on the left correspond to the "embedding" and "1st layer" categories, where the lighter blue bars reach approximately 80 and 82 respectively, and the darker blue bars reach approximately 82 and 82.5. The green bars in the middle section represent random models with a pre-trained embedding layer under various perturbation conditions; the lighter green bars range from approximately 79.5 to 80, while the darker green bars range from approximately 81.5 to 82, with the "random layers +R₂" darker green bar reaching close to 82. The red bars represent random models where the embedding layer is also randomized; the lighter red (pink) bars range from approximately 72 to 72, and the darker red bars range from approximately 73.5 to 74, with the "random" lighter bar at roughly 72 and the "random +R₂" darker bar at approximately 73.5. The final pair of orange bars on the far right, labeled "unperturbed," are notably the tallest, with the lighter orange bar reaching approximately 90.5 and the darker orange bar reaching approximately 92. The bars are not sorted by value but rather grouped by perturbation type and color-coded by model category, with the color scheme progressing from blue to green to red to orange from left to right. The lighter and darker shades within each color group distinguish two variant conditions as described in the legend.
